text:
Nashville brought in Ross Colton to do a third-line job, and so far he is doing it: 8 points (5 goals) in 22 games at about 13 minutes a night, with 52 hits, no power-play points and plenty of speed (his top skating speed ranks in the 96th percentile in NHL EDGE tracking).

His own finishing is about where it should be, five goals on 5.29 expected goals (the quality of his chances). The bad luck sits elsewhere. With him on the ice, the Predators have scored 4.97 fewer goals than their chances deserve, even though they are winning the expected-goals battle at five-on-five (51%). That kind of on-ice shortfall usually swings back, and it has cost him points.

Evolving-Hockey liked his play-driving last season in Colorado (96th percentile among forwards, after adjusting for strong teammates), and the Stanley Cup he won with Tampa Bay in 2021 is a reminder he has filled this role on good teams before. Four of his five goals came in the last ten games. We'd watch whether the assists start to follow the chances.
